newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index continues fall in flat trading.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index continues fall in flat trading.

text.p: The Slovak SAX index continued to fall in sluggish trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday, dragged down by heavy losses to shares of oil and gas storage Nafta.
The 12-share SAX index fell 4.83 points to 174.31 points, with dealers expecting no changes for the better in the immediate future.
"I expect a further decline next week, as I don't see anything which could stop it at the moment," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said.

Nafta fell 333 crowns to 1,327 crowns, but traded only four shares. Steel maker VSZ closed unchanged at 560 crowns, on a volume of 6,000 shares, but Sykora said the issue's price was artificially supported by a 5,000-share block package.
"This block, at some 560 crowns, appeared on the bourse clearly only to keep the price range artificially high," he said.
"Other investors accepted VSZ's price at about 540-545 crowns, which is more realistic, and if this block did not keep it, the price would fall even lower."
Commercial bank VUB was the only blue chip on Friday to gain ground, closing up 23 crowns at 1,691 crowns, with 226 shares traded.
"I think that remaining uncertainty over privatisation of banking sector is the main factor contributing to the relative stability of VUB's price," Sykora added.
Overall volume increased, mainly on direct and block trades, to 597,402 shares, from 410,031 shares traded on Thursday, while turnover eased to 413.04 million crowns, from 449.88 million.
